verdict.line: You lose if he chains a 2-stack Ntofo Strikes pull into Footwork before level 6; you win if you survive to Sunfire/Thornmail and scale through his All Out window.

brief.thesis: K'Sante holds the lane and solo-kill edge because his Q (Ntofo Strikes) pokes on a 3.5s cooldown and pulls you in at 2 stacks, while your own stun setup needs Q's pillar to form before E can knock him up — a slower combo he can just walk away from. The 50.5% win rate over 988 games says it evens out once your tank items and Brittle uptime take over.

theirWindow.when: He's at 1 Q stack near you
theirWindow.what: He's one short-range strike from the pulling shockwave on his Q. Back off to max range or trade with your own Q instead of standing in his Q's short line.

yourWindow.when: Your Q pillar is up, his Footwork is down
yourWindow.what: Dash E (Searing Charge) through the magma pillar for the terrain-collision shockwave knockup, then land the final gout of W (Bellows Breath) for Brittle and free autos before his E shield resets.

powerCurve.note: His low-CD Q poke wins short trades
Your Q-into-pillar E combo comes online
All Out all-in spike is dangerous

start.why: Doran's Shield into Health Potion is the clear pick (50.8% WR, 58.6% pick) — the regen and poke reduction directly answer K'Sante's Q spam, which he'll throw at you every 3.5 seconds from level 1.

boots.why: Plated Steelcaps (51.8% WR, 72.1% pick) cut the auto-attack damage from his Q stacking and his empowered All Out hits, which matter more here than the tenacity on Mercury's Treads since his CC comes in one burst, not a chain.

core.why: Immediate tank stats plus a burn that punishes him for standing in melee range trading Q stacks on you.
Thornmail is the top second item in both measured core paths and directly answers his auto-reset trade pattern and his All Out healing.
Stacks resistances passively through prolonged lane skirmishing and siege phases, which is where this matchup swings back in your favor.

situational.when: his team leans on sustained poke rather than one big burst window
the enemy team shifts toward heavy magic damage alongside him
he's rushing lifesteal or heal-heavy items to abuse his All Out sustain

runes.keystoneWhy: Grasp heals you off autos during the extended trades his Q poke forces, and it triggers naturally once you land the Q-pillar-E knockup and start swinging during W's Brittle window.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport is the dominant pick (50.4% WR, 83% pick) and fits Ornn's scaling plan — Teleport lets you reset back to lane after recalling for forged items instead of walking back through a lane you're not winning early.

playing.title: Zone with Q, don't force E
playing.detail: Poke from Q's 800 range and don't walk E (Searing Charge) in without a wall or an already-formed pillar — a whiffed E just hands him a free Q stack and an easy Footwork punish.

playing.title: Chain Q into the pillar for E
playing.detail: Land Q at trade range, wait for the magma pillar to form, then E through it for the terrain-collision shockwave knockup, and immediately follow with W's final gout for Brittle plus free autos.

playing.title: Respect the double-stack Q
playing.detail: Track his Ntofo Strikes counter — at 2 stacks his Q fires a pulling shockwave. Don't stand in his short-line range when he's one auto from that second stack.

playing.title: Bait his Footwork before all-in
playing.detail: His E (Footwork) is a dash plus shield on a 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s cooldown. Force it out with a Q poke first so the shield is down when you commit your real Q-E combo.

playing.title: Hold Brittle for his All Out
playing.detail: His R (All Out) knocks you through terrain then he dashes in with bonus damage, healing, and transformed abilities for its duration, trading away his own defenses. Save W's Brittle for right after he commits so your team's follow-up hits harder while he's weak.

playing.title: Itemize to outlast, not out-trade
playing.detail: Rush Sunfire Aegis into Thornmail so his Q poke and auto-resets feed your burn and the grief back onto him — the fight swings your way by level 9-13 even though he wins the short trades.

playing.title: Use R to pick your fights
playing.detail: Call of the Forge God sits at a 100s cooldown by rank 3. Summon it to cut off his Footwork dash lane, or recast for the redirect knockup right as his All Out window ends and his defenses are still down.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, rune pages, boots, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning and trade timing are my own read of the kits, not measured data.
